theory.title: Python asyncio.Lock

theory.application: Wrap critical sections with "async with lock:" to prevent state mutation race conditions during DB await operations.
theory.key_characteristics: Ensures thread-safe operations within a single process to prevent concurrent data mutations.

theory.title: TypeScript Mutex

theory.application: Always acquire the mutex before checking or editing global cache records, and release it in a "finally" block.
theory.key_characteristics: Guarantees exclusive access to critical code sections in asynchronous Node.js environments.

interactive_questions.answer: A. PostgreSQL Advisory Locks (e.g., SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(key)).
interactive_questions.explanation: Advisory locks are app-defined database locks that leverage PostgreSQL transaction-scoped locks to block concurrent transactions based on arbitrary application keys, perfect for serverless synchronization.

theory.title: PostgreSQL Advisory Locks
theory.content: Advisory locks let you define custom application locks built directly into PostgreSQL. When using "pg_advisory_xact_lock(key)", the lock is automatically released when the transaction commits or aborts, avoiding manually-managed lock leaks.
theory.analogy: The database acting as an objective referee who hands out numbered passes to represent specific resources.
theory.application: Use advisory locks to protect resources that lack a dedicated physical row (e.g. dynamic external API queues or sequence generation).
theory.key_characteristics: Leverages database-level advisory locks for robust, highly-available synchronization across distributed microservices.
